params.body:
Fixes bevinding de-chassis-modal-post-een-rauw-id. Nightwatch #36.

A dealer opened a sheet on 22 September 2026, used "toevoegen via chassisnummer", and got a 500.

`createFromVIN` reads its parameter with `base64_decode`, because every other link to it is built
with `LinkHelper::route`, which encodes. This one modal built its form action with the plain
`route()` helper and the raw id, so `base64_decode('22992')` produced three random bytes. Those are
not empty, so `filled($vehicle_id)` waved them through, and the vehicle was only looked up much
later, inside `OwnStockService::except_dealers`, where `null->except_dealers()` ended the request.
The modal is included in both classic sheets, so this is an ordinary action, not an odd corner.

Two halves:

- The modal encodes, like its three siblings.
- The id is checked first, before the Outbound gate, because recognising a broken id costs nothing
  and carrying it does. An id that points at no vehicle is a 404 now, the same treatment bevinding
  `verkeerd-id-geeft-500` gave other screens.

Putting the check first made two later defences provably dead, and both are gone rather than left as
decoration: a nullsafe on a vehicle that cannot be null any more, and an `is_null($vehicle)` two
lines after that same vehicle was already dereferenced. Static analysis is clean without adding a
baseline entry.

**What the tests can and cannot show.** They pin the two halves: the modal encodes, and a raw id
answers 404 instead of reaching a service. They cannot reproduce the 500 itself, because outside
production `Outbound::allows('vwe')` refuses the lookup first and the request ends at 422. Against
the code on main the raw id gives that 422, not a crash; the 500 belongs to an environment where the
lookup is allowed. That is written into the finding too, so the next reader does not chase it.
params.title: The chassis modal posts the id the route expects
